items.title: France : un Franco-Algérien à la tête de la contestation lycéenne
items.description: La France est secouée par un mouvement de colère des lycéens qui réclament de meilleures conditions de scolarisation. Au cœur de la contestation, se trouve un Franco-Algérien , Ryad Rani, 19 ans et président de l'Union syndicale lycéenne. Son engagement ne lui épargne, hélas, pas les attaques à caractère raciste. Ryad Rani, fils d’un ouvrier franco-algérien Né à Roubaix d’un père ouvrier franco-algérien et d’une mère française, le jeune homme a connu “une enfance et une adolescence, pas tendres”, avec « des problèmes de santé », comme il le raconte à Radio France. Ses parents se sont séparés et il n’a connu son père que très peu. Sa mère est décédée en janvier dernier et le chagrin ne l’empêche pas de s'investir dans le mouvement en cours dans les lycées de France. Ryad s’est essayé à la politique lors des municipales de mars dernier en se portant candidat sur une liste soutenue par La France Insoumise (LFI) dans la ville où il réside, Wattrelos, dans le Nord. Il rejette toutefois les accusations de “manipulation politique”. “Je ne suis pas encarté dans un parti politique. Je suis syndicaliste. Oui, je fais de la politique parce que ça a un lien ! Forcément quand on a des revendications comme celles du mouvement qu'on a aujourd'hui, on fait forcément de la politique”, dit-il. “Les mêmes chances pour tous les lycéens de France” Élu au printemps dernier à la tête du syndicat des lycéens, il s’est retrouvé après seulement quelques mois au cœur d’un mouvement de contestation d'ampleur, qu'il encourage et qu'il contribue à encadrer. Dénonçant les “violences policières”, il estime que, “quand on voit que dans le pays des droits de l'Homme, on éborgne des lycéens, c'est d'une violence inouïe”. Partisan d'une contestation pacifique, il a appelé les lycéens à être “prudents et à ne pas provoquer les forces de l'ordre”. Le Franco-Algérien veut les mêmes chances partout et pour tous les lycéens, “dans les beaux quartiers de Paris” et “à Montpellier, Marseille ou Mayotte”. Attaques racistes et menaces de mort Ce qui l'amène à s’engager à fond dans le mouvement ? La situation dans les lycées de France où, décrit-il, “il y a des plafonds qui ne tiennent plus, pas de rideau, des inondations, des portiques qui ne fonctionnent plus”, ou encore un manque de professeurs dans plusieurs spécialités et une surcharge des classes. Le jeune homme est déterminé. “Nous avons une dignité et nous ne nous plierons pas à des négociations dans les salons ministériels. Déjà, on demande de la considération”, dit-il. Comme de nombreux Franco-Algériens, Ryad Rani n’échappe pas au racisme ambiant. Pas loin que cette semaine, il assure qu'il a été victime de nombreuses insultes racistes et de menaces de mort. En plus d’avoir des origines algériennes, le courant extrémiste a une autre raison de s’en prendre à lui. Il est pleinement engagé dans le combat politique contre cette mouvance. “Je me refuse de rester les bras croisés, quand je vois ma ville, mon département, ma région ou mon pays qui risquent de tomber à l'extrême droite », explique-t-il sa candidature aux dernières municipales. items.title: Inflation to average 11.3% in 2027 – Fitch Solutions
items.description: Fitch Solutions has predicted an upward inflation in 2027, from an annual average of 4.7% in 2026 to 11.3% in 2027. This will be driven by fading exchange rate support, modest fiscal loosening and strong money supply growth, with broad money supply growth already exceeding nominal Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth by 17.1 percentage points in quarter two 2026. In addition, the UK-based firm said the strong El Niño event, which will peak towards the end of 2026, has already begun lifting global food prices and will likely add to imported inflationary pressures in Ghana during 2027. “As inflation accelerates and breaches the 10% mark in Q2 [quarter 2 2027], we expect the BoG to begin tightening, raising the policy rate by a cumulative 200bps [200 basis points] by year-end”, it explained. It pointed out that a further escalation and/or more prolonged tensions in the Middle East would push energy prices higher, keeping fuel costs elevated in Ghana and adding to inflation. This could prompt the Bank of Ghana to tighten as early as November 2026 or deliver more than the 200 basis points of hikes Fitch Solutions currently forecast. It also forecasts that the current account surplus will narrow from 7.9% of GDP in 2026 to 5.3% in 2027, reflecting a modest decline in gold prices from US$4,400/oz to U$$4,200/oz and a 9.1% decline in cocoa production due to El Niño-related weather disruptions. Moreover, with the Bank of Ghana explicitly targeting 15 months of import cover by 2028 – a goal Fitch Solutions views as highly ambitious and unlikely to be reached – policymakers will likely seek to maintain a positive real interest rate to support portfolio investment inflows.

items.title: ‘I didn’t campaign for NDC to come and do this nonsense’ – Kpebu on EOCO’s conduct
items.description: Private legal practitioner Martin Kpebu has expressed disappointment with the conduct of some National Democratic Congress (NDC) appointees, saying he did not support the party in the 2024 elections for them to engage in what he described as “nonsense”. Speaking in an interview amid the ongoing controversy involving the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) and Manhyia South MP Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah, Mr Kpebu alleged that some government appointees were misusing their legal authority and damaging the image of the governing party. “It is a shame, I didn’t campaign for the NDC to come and do this nonsense,” he said. Mr Kpebu said he had campaigned vigorously for the NDC, adding that supporting the party during the administration of former President Nana Akufo-Addo had not been easy. “Do you know how we suffered? Akufo-Addo, do you know how dangerous he was? Do you know what we lost?” he argued. “Then you (NDC) come, this is how you are misusing the power?” he lamented. He said those experiences made the conduct he was witnessing particularly painful, having worked to support the party’s return to power. Mr Kpebu’s criticism centred on what he considered an improper use of legal authority by some appointees and the potential consequences for public confidence in the NDC administration. He also warned that EOCO’s actions and inactions could carry an electoral cost for the governing party, arguing that the agency’s conduct could contribute to the NDC losing power in the 2028 general election.

items.title: Gunmen kill one, injure seven Plateau traders
items.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — Gunmen on Sunday evening opened fire on traders returning from the Kara Bukuru Livestock Market in Jos South Local Government Area of Plateau State, killing one person and injuring seven others. The victim was identified as Musa Abubakar. The incident occurred at about 7pm around the Bukuru Low-Cost area, according to sources who spoke to our correspondent. The Plateau State chapter of the Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association of Nigeria, MACBAN, confirmed and condemned the attack, calling on security agencies to investigate the incident and bring those responsible to justice. In a statement signed by its chairman, Alhaji Ibrahim Yusuf Babayo, MACBAN described the incident as disturbing, saying the victims were returning from their lawful business activities. “This unfortunate incident is deeply disturbing and represents yet another attack against innocent herders who were peacefully returning from their lawful business activities,” Babayo said. He urged the Nigeria Police Force, Operation Safe Haven, the Department of State Services, DSS, and other security agencies to conduct a thorough investigation into the incident. Babayo recalled that five herders were reportedly killed on September 20, 2026, around Kassa in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area while returning from the same Kara Bukuru Livestock Market. He also recalled that traders were attacked near the Conoil Filling Station in December last year while returning from the market. According to him, the recurrence of such incidents had heightened fear and insecurity among pastoralists and traders who depend on the market for their livelihoods. “No Nigerian should be attacked or killed because of his or her ethnic background or occupation,” he said. The MACBAN chairman called on the Plateau State Government and security agencies to strengthen security along the Kara Bukuru market route and take measures to prevent further attacks. He also appealed to members of the association to remain calm and law-abiding and refrain from any form of retaliation. Babayo said MACBAN remained committed to peaceful coexistence with communities across Plateau State, stressing that lasting peace could only be achieved through justice, fairness and equal protection of citizens irrespective of ethnicity or occupation. The post Gunmen kill one, injure seven Plateau traders appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: INEC to update Nigerians on 2027 polls
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, will on Tuesday update Nigerians on preparations for the 2027 general election as the country marks 100 days to the polls. The Commission said it would provide updates on the voters’ register, candidate nominations, logistics and measures being put in place to safeguard the integrity of the electoral process. The update will be given at a World Press Conference scheduled for October 6, 2026, alongside a National Stakeholders’ Meeting in Abuja. In a statement by its Chief Press Secretary and Media Adviser to the INEC Chairman, Adedayo Oketola, the Commission said the briefing would focus on key aspects of its preparations for the elections. The statement said INEC “will provide updates on preparations for the elections, including the voters’ register, candidate nominations, logistics and critical measures to ensure the integrity of the electoral process.” The press conference will be addressed by the INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria, alongside other key stakeholders involved in the electoral process. The event will be held at the Bola Ahmed Tinubu International Conference Centre, BAT-ICC, Abuja. The National Stakeholders’ Meeting is expected to bring together political party leaders, security agencies under the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security, ICCES, members of the diplomatic corps, development partners, civil society organisations and election observer groups. Also expected are disability rights advocates, religious and traditional leaders, youth organisations and media executives. According to INEC, the engagement is part of efforts to strengthen transparency and communication ahead of the elections and ensure broader participation by stakeholders in the electoral process. The Commission said the meeting “underlines the Commission’s commitment to absolute transparency, proactive public communication, and collaborative engagement with key actors in the electoral ecosystem.” The post INEC to update Nigerians on 2027 polls appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Insecurity must not become Nigeria’s new normal — Obi
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, has called for the immediate and safe rescue of about 20 prospective members of the National Youth Service Corps, NYSC, reportedly abducted while travelling to their orientation camp. Obi, in a post on his official social media page on Sunday, described the reported abduction as another indication of what he called worsening insecurity in the country, warning that Nigerians should not accept insecurity as a normal part of everyday life. The former Anambra State governor said the victims were young Nigerians travelling to serve their country but were unable to complete their journey safely because of insecurity on the nation’s roads. He said the incident had also heightened anxiety among families whose loved ones travel across the country for work, education and national assignments. “The abduction of approximately 20 prospective NYSC members travelling to their orientation camp is yet another distressing indication of the worsening insecurity in our country. “These young Nigerians were preparing to serve their nation, but they were unable to travel safely on our roads. Families are increasingly burdened by the fear that their loved ones could fall victim to kidnapping,” Obi said. The 2023 presidential candidate of the Labour Party, LP, said protecting lives and property remained a primary responsibility of government. He urged security agencies to intensify efforts to prevent attacks and respond promptly to threats rather than waiting until lives had been disrupted. “Protecting lives and property is the government’s foremost responsibility. We cannot continue to regard insecurity as an ordinary occurrence or act only after people’s lives have been disrupted,” he said. Obi called on security agencies to intensify efforts to locate and rescue the abducted prospective corps members and apprehend those responsible for the attack. “I call for the immediate and safe rescue of all the abducted corps members and the arrest of those responsible. Nigeria must become a country where young people can travel, work, and serve their nation without fear,” he said. The reported abduction has renewed concerns over the safety of travellers on Nigerian highways, particularly young Nigerians travelling to unfamiliar locations for national assignments. The NYSC, established in 1973, was designed, among other objectives, to promote national integration by deploying graduates to states outside their states of origin for one year of national service. However, recurring reports of kidnappings and attacks on major highways have continued to raise concerns about the safety of corps members and other travellers across the country. The post Insecurity must not become Nigeria’s new normal — Obi appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Fitch Solutions maintains policy rate forecast of 14% by December 2026
items.description: Fitch Solutions has maintained its policy rate forecast at 14.00% by year-end, before the Bank of Ghana hikes it by 200 basis points (bps) to 16.00% in 2027. This follows the unchanged policy rate of 14% by the Bank of Ghana at the recent Monetary Policy Committee (MPC meeting. According to the UK-based firm, persistent single-digit inflation drives will compel the Bank of Ghana to keep the benchmark policy rate unchanged at the final MPC meeting of 2026 in November. “Consumer price growth has remained at multi-decade lows this year, averaging just 4.0% year-on-year, well below the 2010-2025 average of 15.7% and the BoG’s 6.0-10.0% target range. Price pressures have been contained by the lagged effects of earlier monetary tightening, favourable base effects and a stronger cedi from a year-on-year perspective”, it said in its macro insight on Ghana. It continued that inflation has nevertheless risen from 3.2% in March 2026 to 5.0% in August 2026, and “we expect it to continue trending higher, reaching 6.8% by year-end”. This primarily reflects elevated energy costs amid the ongoing US-Iran conflict and the cedi starting to weaken on a year-on-year basis. Even so, it pointed out that inflation will remain low by Ghanaian standards and below the BoG’s target midpoint through quarter 4, 2026, limiting the need for monetary tightening. Meanwhile, with inflation moving higher, the UK-based firm see little appetite for rate cuts, making another hold in November 2026 the most likely outcome.

items.title: What is fuelling school protests in France?
items.description: Protests by teenagers outside their schools have shaken France in recent days, with students blockading entrances to their institutions and security forces on occasion responding with tear gas. The government has said that while the grievances may be legitimate, violence is not and has accused the hard-left of whipping up the movement. Critics have meanwhile accused some police of heavy-handed force against protesters, who are legally still children. More than 5,000 people have been arrested since Monday, according to the interior ministry, while about 735 educational establishments were affected on Friday, the education minister said. While the weekend may see a lull, a major new day of protest is planned for Tuesday. AFP looks at the origins of the movement. Multiple grievances The protests affect lycees, the schools where French teens have their last years of school, aged from 15-18, the equivalent of high school in the United States and sixth form in the United Kingdom. The students’ grievances are numerous, but chief among them are teacher absences, conditions in classrooms, overloaded school timetables and a school day that can be as long as 8:00am to 6:00pm, which some say is excessive. “High-school students — particularly those from low-income neighbourhoods — feel they are receiving an inferior education,” said French sociologist Valerie Becquet. A student puts trash into a fire as protesting students carry out blockading action near place de la Nation, in Paris, on Oct 2, 2026. — AFP Origin of the movement The movement began two weeks ago on Sept 17 at the Saint-Exupéry high school in the Paris suburb of Créteil, in support of teachers striking over a lack of staff and resources. It gained momentum, gradually spreading across the country over the last week. Ironically, as tensions raged elsewhere in France, the situation at the Saint-Exupery high school returned to normal after educational authorities agreed to send additional staff, including a deputy principal and a nurse. “Our grades were slipping. If we had not rallied now it would have augured very badly for the future,” said pupil Abderrahmane, who expressed “enormous” pride at taking part in the inception of the movement. Mayor of Metz Francois Grosdidier (L) stands in front of burned vehicles belonging to staff members during a visit, at the Francois Rabelais secondary school, after the fire started last evening during students’ blockading action protest in Metz, northeastern France on Oct 3, 2026. — AFP Role of social media The protests are being further fuelled by the spread of dramatic images and videos on online platforms, notably TikTok. Students themselves hold up their phones to record scenes such as burning trash cans or police deploying tear gas. Numerous channels, seeking to boost their reach, spread this footage and edit together the most dramatic moments. “With social media, they can offer a narrative different from the one presented in traditional media — a narrative that is not manufactured,” said sociologist Becquet. Social inequality France offers all students access to the lycee but in reality there is a vast spectrum, ranging from vocational schools to elite institutions. Despite numerous diversity initiatives, the latter remain dominated by students from white, affluent families with university-educated parents. “There are glaring inequalities among different students and schools, and this is a real problem,” said Becquet. Political exploitation The protests have become a major issue of political tension just over half a year ahead of presidential elections, with the government accusing the hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) of being behind the movement. Senior LFI official Manuel Bompard has rejected the government’s accusations, saying it was “descending into conspiracy theories”. Veteran LFI presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon — who is currently polling at over 40 per cent among 18-25-year-old voters — has strongly supported the protests, while calling for non-violent methods. Police response Protesters have blockaded schools, set fire to bins and other objects and hurled projectiles at police. But police have also moved to disperse some of the protesters, notably firing tear gas canisters, using rubber bullets and sometimes beating them with batons. After students clashed with police on Wednesday in Tours in central France, one young man wounded lost the use of his right eye, the city’s prosecutor said. Numerous videos have gone viral showing alleged brutal conduct by security forces — such as a police officer placing his arm around the neck of a girl during her arrest. But police have also been targets, notably an officer who was chased and beaten and kicked by a group of youths from a school in the eastern city of Belfort. Header image: French high school students block access to the Lycee Paul Eluard high school as they protest to demand the hiring of substitute teachers, increased resources and better learning conditions, in Saint-Denis, near Paris, France, on Sept 30, 2026. — Reuters

items.title: Welfare Concerns: Nine Zamfara lawmakers dump APC
items.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau Nine members of the Zamfara State House of Assembly have dumped the All Progressives Congress, APC, citing what they described as a lack of concern for the welfare of the people and disagreements over insecurity in the state. One of the lawmakers, Aliyu Ango Kagara, who represents Talata-Mafara South, said their disagreements with Governor Dauda Lawal were largely rooted in the security challenges confronting the state and what he described as the government’s inadequate response to the plight of residents. Kagara said the lawmakers raised concerns about insecurity on the floor of the Assembly, but their position did not go down well with the governor, leading to disagreements and their subsequent suspension. “Because of the lack of security and lack of concern for the people of Zamfara, we raised the issue in the House, which did not go down well with the governor. “That was why we had issues with him, which led to our suspension and later dumping of APC,” Kagara said. The lawmaker, however, alleged that their grievances persisted, claiming that some party leaders conspired against them and denied them a fair hearing. The lawmakers include Kagara, representing Talata-Mafara South; Muktar Nasir, popularly known as Jikan Shehu, representing Kaura Namoda North; Faruk Dosara Musa, representing Maradun I; and Basiru Bello, representing Bungudu West. Others are Barrister Bashir A. Masama, representing Bukkuyum North; Ibrahim T. Tukur, representing Bakura; Nasiru Abdullahi, representing Maru North; Yusuf Muhammad Anka, representing Anka; and Rt. Hon. Bashar Aliyu, representing Gummi I. The development comes amid continuing political disagreements in Zamfara over the handling of insecurity and other governance issues in the state. The post Welfare Concerns: Nine Zamfara lawmakers dump APC appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Umahi tackles ‘emergency social media engineers’ over Coastal Highway flooding claims
items.description: Minister of Works, David Umahi, has dismissed claims linking the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway to flooding in communities along its corridor, blaming the situation on climate change and global warming. Umahi said the flooding in the affected areas predated the highway’s construction, arguing that the project should not be held responsible for a problem he described as a consequence of changing weather patterns. The minister spoke on Sunday during an interview on Channels Television, where he also criticised social media users for making claims about the project without adequate technical knowledge. “The Coastal Highway has nothing to do with flooding,” Umahi said, adding that infrastructure built decades ago had not been designed to accommodate the effects of climate change and global warming. He explained that unusual flooding was not peculiar to Nigeria, citing his experience in Paris, France, where he said some buildings had experienced severe flooding, forcing occupants to relocate their ground-floor activities to higher levels. “At the coastal highway corridor, the premises were built below the unexpected flood level occasioned by global warming, the climate change,” he said. Umahi argued that flooding had occurred in communities along the highway corridor before construction began, insisting that the project was not the cause of the problem. “Before the construction of Coastal Highway, was there flooding within that premises? The answer is yes,” he said. The minister challenged critics to consider the impact of climate change and the occurrence of unusual flooding across the country before attributing the problem to the highway. He also questioned why flooding was being reported in areas on both sides of the coastal road if the project was responsible for the situation. “The Coastal Highway has nothing to do with the flooding. Otherwise, if it is what is causing the flooding, why is there flooding left and right of the Coastal Highway?” he asked. Umahi described the highway as a significant infrastructure project and took aim at critics he accused of commenting on its impact without sufficient technical understanding. “It’s a beauty to behold, and so people just started counselling without knowledge. You see that there are emergency engineers these days, people just talk on social media anyhow,” he said. The post Umahi tackles ‘emergency social media engineers’ over Coastal Highway flooding claims appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: La Téranga au défi de l’altérité !
items.description: 1. Introduction : L'altérité Le Sénégal, historiquement sanctuarisé comme la terre de la Teranga, traverse une zone de turbulences où ses fondements mêmes vacillent sous le poids de pathologies identitaires émergentes. Cette tradition séculaire de brassage humain est aujourd'hui confrontée à une myopie historique préoccupante, marquée par la montée de discours xénophobes qui visent nos frères et sœurs d'Afrique de l'Ouest. Nous assistons à un glissement périlleux : le débat légitime sur la gestion des flux migratoires et les défaillances de l'administration publique est instrumentalisé pour basculer dans une stigmatisation systématique de l'Autre. L'enjeu majeur : Comment préserver le pacte social et l'intégrité de notre nation quand l'étranger, autrefois figure sacrée de l'hôte, est transmuté en bouc émissaire de nos propres insuffisances structurelles ? La frontière entre la vigilance républicaine et la haine identitaire est devenue si poreuse qu'elle menace de rompre l'équilibre de notre cohésion nationale. Pour désamorcer cette dynamique délétère, il est impératif de déconstruire les récits de division et de rappeler que nos frontières actuelles ne sont que des cicatrices récentes sur un corps social millénaire. 2. L'Ancienneté des Liens : Quand l'Histoire ignore les Frontières Vouloir isoler le Sénégal de son environnement immédiat relève d'un anachronisme sociopolitique. Les peuples de notre sous-région, notamment les Peuls (Fulɓe), forment une unité culturelle et linguistique — le Pulaar ou Fulfulde — qui tisse un pont vivant entre plus de vingt pays. Historiquement, le Fouta-Toro et le Fouta-Djallon n'étaient pas des entités étrangères l'une à l'autre, mais les deux poumons d'un même organisme historique. Avant que la colonisation n'impose ses découpages administratifs, quatre réseaux fondamentaux assuraient la fluidité de cet espace : ● Réseaux religieux : La constitution des États musulmans aux XVIIIe et XIXe siècles a favorisé l'émergence de véritables « communautés épistémiques », où la circulation des savants et des manuscrits ignorait les distances. ● Réseaux familiaux : Des siècles de transhumance et d'alliances matrimoniales ont créé une toile de parenté si dense que la notion de « nationalité » pure devient une fiction biologique. ● Réseaux commerciaux : Les circuits marchands et pastoraux ont structuré l'économie de la Sénégambie et du Mali bien avant l'avènement des douanes modernes. ● Réseaux intellectuels : La mobilité des élites lettrées a forgé un socle de valeurs partagées, garantissant une continuité de pensée de Dakar à Conakry. L'indépendance de la Guinée en 1958 n'a pas créé une nouvelle migration, mais a simplement inscrit dans un cadre post-colonial une continuité de mouvements organiques. Les frontières héritées sont des superpositions administratives sur une réalité humaine préexistante, nous imposant de repenser la nationalité non comme une barrière, mais comme une composante d'un héritage partagé. 3. L'Interdépendance Économique : Un Destin Commun Le repli sur soi est une illusion suicidaire dans un monde globalisé. Au sein de la CEDEAO, la libre circulation n'est pas une concession généreuse, mais le carburant de notre croissance collective. Le Sénégal, loin d'être une île, est le bénéficiaire direct d'un marché régional intégré. Mythes vs Réalités Économiques Mythes Xénophobes, Réalités Factuelles « » »Les étrangers accaparent nos ressources. » » », »Les immigrés sont des investisseurs locaux, créateurs de marchés et contributeurs fiscaux essentiels à la dynamique urbaine. » « » »L'immigration est la source de la précarité. » » », »Le chômage et l'inflation découlent de choix politiques et de contraintes structurelles, et non de la présence de voisins africains. » « » »Le protectionnisme garantit la souveraineté. » » »,La souveraineté réelle est régionale. Le Sénégal dépend vitalement de partenaires comme le Mali ; déstabiliser la confiance avec un voisin (ex: la Guinée) fragilise tout l'écosystème CEDEAO. La prospérité de notre pays est intrinsèquement liée à sa capacité à demeurer ce carrefour d'échanges qu'il a toujours été. La fragmentation de cet espace ne ferait qu'appauvrir l'ensemble des acteurs. 4. Les Signaux d'Alerte : Du Langage à la Déshumanisation L'ingénierie de la haine suit un protocole universel que l'histoire nous commande de reconnaître. Les tragédies de l'Allemagne nazie, du Rwanda ou les crises sud-africaines ne sont pas nées spontanément ; elles ont été préparées par la « normalisation » du discours de rejet. Le passage de l'acte individuel (une fraude documentaire, par exemple) au stigmate collectif est le déclencheur de la déshumanisation. Les trois étapes clés de cette fracture sociale sont : La corruption du langage : L'usage de termes déshumanisants (« parasites », « envahisseurs ») transforme un groupe humain en une pathologie à traiter, anesthésiant ainsi la vigilance démocratique. L'amalgame et la généralisation : C'est ici que l'individu disparaît derrière la communauté. On ne juge plus un délit, on condamne une origine. C'est le mécanisme même qui a permis le passage des lois de Nuremberg (exclusion institutionnelle) à la violence de masse. La déshumanisation sociale : Inspirée par les rhétoriques de type « Radio Mille Collines », cette phase rend l'agression socialement acceptable, voire nécessaire, aux yeux d'une population dont on a saturé l'esprit de peurs irrationnelles. Face à ces mécanismes, la seule réponse viable réside dans une réaffirmation intransigeante des valeurs républicaines et de la dignité humaine. 5. Note d'alerte institutionnelle : Mesures pour un Patriotisme Civique Pour stopper l'érosion de notre cohésion sociale, l'État et la société civile doivent coordonner une réponse systémique. Voici les piliers de cette ingénierie de la résilience : Justice et Application de la Loi ● Fermeté impartiale : L'État doit sanctionner les fraudes administratives ou commerciales avec rigueur, mais sans distinction d'origine. La sanction doit demeurer individuelle pour ne jamais nourrir le discrédit collectif. C'est le pilier de la confiance envers les institutions. ● Sécurité juridique : Garantir que tout étranger en situation régulière jouisse d'une protection totale, réaffirmant ainsi que le Sénégal est un État de droit et non de privilèges ethniques. Régulation des Médias et Numérique ● Lutte contre l'infodémie de la haine : Mettre en place une veille rigoureuse contre la désinformation sur les réseaux sociaux. La liberté d'expression ne saurait couvrir l'incitation à la violence ou le harcèlement communautaire. ● Responsabilisation des leaders d'opinion : Inciter les autorités religieuses et coutumières à porter un discours de désamorçage, car la parole publique est le premier rempart contre la barbarie. Éducation et Dialogue ● Promotion du Métissage Universel : mieux intégrer dans les programmes scolaires l'histoire de la longue durée (Empire du Mali, Sénégambie) pour démontrer que notre diversité est notre structure fondamentale. ● Comités locaux de veille citoyenne : Créer des espaces de médiation de proximité pour détecter les tensions locales et les résoudre par le dialogue avant qu'elles ne soient instrumentalisées par des entrepreneurs de la haine. 6. Conclusion : Choisir le Métissage Universel Le métissage universel n'est pas une abdication de la souveraineté, mais la célébration de notre identité profonde. De l'Empire du Mali aux espaces de circulation de la Sénégambie, l'histoire nous enseigne que les sociétés les plus résilientes sont celles qui transforment leur pluralité en levier de puissance. Une nation forte n'est pas celle qui cherche la pureté dans l'exclusion, mais celle qui reconnaît en chaque étranger un miroir de sa propre trajectoire historique. Le Sénégal doit choisir son modèle : celui du repli et de la peur, ou celui de l'ouverture et de l'intelligence collective. La force d'une nation réside dans sa capacité à transformer sa diversité en richesse commune, garantissant à chaque individu, quelle que soit son origine, une égalité de dignité devant la loi. Cercle de réflexion sur le Sénégal : Xeltu sunum Rew

items.title: Décès de Cheikh Hamidou Kane : le président béninois Romuald Wadagni rend hommage à l’auteur de « L’Aventure ambiguë »
items.description: Le président de la République du Bénin, Romuald Wadagni, a rendu hommage à l’écrivain sénégalais Cheikh Hamidou Kane, décédé samedi à Dakar à l’âge de 98 ans. Il salue la mémoire d’une figure de la génération des indépendances et l’héritage de l’auteur de « L’Aventure ambiguë ». Les hommages continuent d’affluer après la disparition de l’écrivain sénégalais Cheikh Hamidou Kane. Au Bénin, le président de la République, Romuald Wadagni, a exprimé sa « profonde tristesse » après l’annonce du décès de l’auteur de « L’Aventure ambiguë », survenu samedi 3 octobre à Dakar, à l’âge de 98 ans. Dans un message publié dimanche, le chef de l’État béninois a salué en Cheikh Hamidou Kane « une grande voix de la génération des indépendances ». Il a également souligné la contribution de l’écrivain à la réflexion sur l’Afrique, notamment sur les questions d’identité, de culture et de rapport au monde. Pour Romuald Wadagni, l’œuvre de Cheikh Hamidou Kane dépasse les frontières du Sénégal. « L’Aventure ambiguë restera l’une de ces œuvres qui traversent les époques et continuent de nous interroger », a-t-il écrit, en référence au roman publié en 1961 et devenu un classique de la littérature africaine. L’ouvrage, traduit dans plus d’une quarantaine de langues, a marqué plusieurs générations de lecteurs par sa réflexion sur la rencontre entre les savoirs, les cultures et les identités africaines. « Le Sénégal perd un grand écrivain. L’Afrique perd une grande voix », a poursuivi le président béninois, qui a adressé ses condoléances à la famille du défunt, à ses proches, au peuple sénégalais ainsi qu’à l’ensemble de la communauté littéraire. Cet hommage vient s’ajouter à ceux rendus au Sénégal à l’écrivain et ancien ministre. Le président Bassirou Diomaye Faye a notamment salué la mémoire d’un « serviteur du Sénégal », estimant que son œuvre appartient désormais au patrimoine de la Nation et de toute l’Afrique. Né le 2 avril 1928 à Matam, Cheikh Hamidou Kane avait également mené une carrière dans la haute administration et occupé plusieurs fonctions publiques. Son parcours associait ainsi littérature, service de l’État et réflexion sur les sociétés africaines. En conclusion de son hommage, Romuald Wadagni a prié pour que le défunt bénéficie de la miséricorde divine, tout en soulignant la pérennité de son héritage : « Reposez en paix. Votre œuvre continuera de vivre. »

items.title: Le projet de Loi de finances 2027 adopté : Tebboune intègre la hausse des salaires
items.description: Le projet de Loi de finances (PLF) 2027 , dont les grands axes ont été dévoilés mercredi 30 septembre, a été adopté ce dimanche en Conseil des ministres qui s’est réuni sous la présidence du président Abdelmadjid Tebboune. « Le président de la République a ordonné l'inclusion des augmentations de salaires – conformément à ses engagements envers les Algériennes et les Algériens – dans le projet de Loi de finances 2027 », a indiqué la Présidence de la République dans un communiqué. « Je me suis engagé à parachever l’augmentation de 53 % des salaires et je réitère cet engagement. Le versement de ces augmentations se fera à partir de l’année 2027. Si les conditions le permettent, cette mesure sera appliquée en une seule tranche, dans le cas contraire, elle se concrétisera en deux tranches », a déclaré le chef de l’État lors de son entrevue périodique avec les médias nationaux samedi soir. Projet de Loi de finances 2027 : Tebboune ne veut pas de nouvelles taxes Le chef de l’État a ordonné de « ne pas inclure de taxe susceptible de porter atteinte au pouvoir d'achat des citoyens, qu'il s'agisse de la classe moyenne ou des personnes à revenus limités ». L’avant-projet de Loi de finances 2027 a été examiné mercredi 30 septembre par le gouvernement lors de sa réunion hebdomadaire. items.title: Naqvi says talks with opposition have collapsed, accuses KP CM of 'sabotaging' negotiations
items.description: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said on Sunday that the talks between the federal government and the opposition had collapsed as the PTI had initiated its long march, accusing Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi of “sabotaging” the negotiations. Naqvi was addressing a press conference in Lahore after an hours-long second round of talks between the two sides ended without yielding any results. “Their team was reasonable. I am repeating that I will not blame anyone else for all of this collapsing. There is only one person responsible for the entire collapse, and that is the KP chief minister,” the interior minister declared. He further said that Afridi was to be responsible “if there is any loss of life”. He said those supporting the PTI leader should “realise that they will be committing contempt of court, and we will take legal action against them to every possible extent”. He warned that no one would be allowed to violate the Islamabad High Court’s order regarding protest. The IHC order , issued on Sept 14, ruled that no political party or its leadership has the “lawful right to occupy public roads, highways, interchanges, toll plazas and buildings in Islamabad”. Notably, Naqvi stressed that there “had been no request from our side for the long march to be postponed”. “When we had the first meeting, we told them that the long march was not an issue for us. However, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto had already given an indication and had also given a date. A day earlier, he had said that the PPP wanted the long march to be postponed and for the temperature to be brought down,” he added. Naqvi explained that the PTI was given the option to hold a protest but would not allow an attempt to “create a disturbance”. “We gave them this option. Now, if they violate the orders, whether they are workers or politicians, whether they are protesting within KP or outside KP, we will pursue them one by one. This time, we want to ensure that this repeated episode of creating a disturbance in Islamabad comes to an end,” he asserted. According to the interior minister, there were two agreements to be reached — one was a “main agreement” that would cover whatever was being decided with the opposition parties, and the other was regarding counterterrorism. “If we had known that no one in this committee was authorised to give a commitment on behalf of the KP government, or that the KP government would veto all these things, we would not have held the negotiations in this form in the first place,” he remarked. The minister said the two sides had agreed “100 per cent on political things” so that the KP government could come on board with the Centre on the counterterrorism issues. “It is not appropriate that there is a war going on in one province and the ministers there are giving statements against the army, are not coming to funerals, and at the local level, somewhere or the other, terrorists are also being given support,” he added. “If there is a military operation, would you tell the army which gun to use or which drone to use? This happens nowhere in the world,” he said. Naqvi detailed Saturday’s developments: “I requested CM Afridi to onboard the KP government because, definitely, the problems we are facing are coming from the KP government. He said, ‘Okay, I am going now,’ so we postponed the meeting until tomorrow. All members agreed to the postponement. “They (opposition team) held negotiations with CM Afridi for four hours. The KP CM gave them his feedback and gave them the mandate that whatever they finalise with him, they should proceed with it.” The interior minister accused Afridi of changing the draft of the agreement despite what had been agreed to earlier. “When I forwarded the draft to the KP chief minister, around 9pm he became active. Once the draft is finalised, he asks for changes once and then asks again, and by 12am or 12:30am at night, he brings an entirely new draft. And in that, he changed the things that we had locked after discussing them,” Naqvi asserted. In an apparent jibe at the KP CM, Naqvi noted that placing “immature and inexperienced people in positions of authority had consequences for the country”. “You have seen in the past how chief ministers came to this province and the country continued to suffer the consequences. Similarly, if an immature boy sits in a position of authority, has no experience and has not seen politics, then definitely he will call himself a representative of the people, but he will make decisions in the same way as my team and I witnessed yesterday.” Commending the government’s delegation, the minister said: “They worked non-stop for 12 hours and, even before that, made sincere efforts to resolve the issue. I will give them credit for the fact that at no point did they say no. They remained focused on resolving the matter. From the smallest issue to the major ones, all the members made a sincere effort to resolve them in a good manner.” Naqvi meets Kundi at Governor House Naqvi then went to Peshawar, where he met KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi. According to a statement issued by the Governor House, both leaders expressed concerns over the “risk of facilitating terrorists to safely cross security checkposts” during the PTI’s Islamabad march. They agreed that whenever the president and the prime minister deemed it necessary to impose governor’s rule or emergency to “save the province from terrorism and destruction, the Governor’s House will play a full Constitutional role”. The interior minister and the governor discussed important matters at the provincial level, including growing unrest in the province, the political scenario, and the situation arising from the Islamabad march. The statement read that the KP government’s attitude during the negotiation regarding counterterrorism actions was tantamount to enmity toward the people and the province. Naqvi and Kundi also termed the use of helicopters and other government resources by Afridi and the provincial ministers for the march as a “blatant violation” of the IHC verdict. Other matters of mutual interest were also discussed in the meeting, and consultations were held on numerous issues, according to the statement. Kundi said in his own statement that KP Inspector General of Police Zulfikar Hameed was also present at the meeting, which revolved around the prevailing security situation in the province. “The security of our people remains our foremost priority. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has sacrificed enough, and every institution must work together to protect our people and defeat terrorism,” the governor said. Earlier in the day, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif visited Naqvi’s residence to offer condolences over the death of his maternal uncle, Akmal Hussain Naqvi. According to the PM Office, the interior minister also briefed PM Shehbaz in detail on the “key negotiations held last night and the progress made” so far. PM Shehbaz also met with PML-N President Nawaz Sharif to discuss the “overall political situation in the country”, state broadcaster Radio Pakistan reported . Matters of international importance were also discussed during the meeting, which was attended by Punjab CM Maryam Nawaz as well, the report added. Conditions and demands Earlier in the day, Naqvi also claimed on X that the KP government had agreed to sign a written agreement and submit an implementation plan within 72 hours, mainly covering counterterrorism initiatives, during the talks held over the weekend, but then backtracked. According to Naqvi, the PTI had agreed to: Reconsider the Police Act 2026 in light of the security situation and the need to protect security matters from political interference Prevent terrorists from operating freely or finding safe havens in the province Unequivocal condemnation of the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan and all other terrorist groups Support the national policy on Afghan refugees, including repatriation and dismantling Afghan camps in KP No contact with the interim Afghan government Substantial funding for counterterrorism operations and the police Full provincial ownership of counterterrorism measures and stronger cooperation with the armed forces Decisions on counterterrorism in the former Fata and merged districts Implementation of the National Action Plan “Last night, during the final phase of negotiations, the KP government backed out of these commitments. Security must not be politicised while the province is at war,” he said. The meeting between the opposition and federal government at Parliament House began after 4pm on Saturday, with discussions focusing on the PTI’s planned Oct 4 march to Islamabad. The talks extended into the early hours of Sunday without yielding any results. However, shortly before 3am on Sunday, Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, who was part of the opposition delegation, told the media that the talks had not resulted in a breakthrough. He went on to say that the deadlock was over jailed PTI founder Imran Khan’s meeting with his personal physicians, and how to address terrorism in KP. But Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry, who was part of the government’s delegation, said the talks failed primarily because the “KP government could not assure whether they would cooperate in the fight against terrorism in the future”. He alleged that the PTI’s provincial government in KP did not want to implement the NAP and that the PTI delegation that participated in the talks had also left the venue “disappointed because the KP government did not cooperate on terrorism”. Following these allegations, CM Afridi posted on X that he was sharing the text of the draft he sent to the opposition’s negotiating team, saying that “no even one demand in there was unconstitutional or illegal”. He then went on to list the demands, calling for: Arrangements for meetings between the prime minister and the leaders of the opposition in both houses of Parliament to discuss important political, national, constitutional, legal, and democratic issues, particularly those facing delays. “The two sides shall be bound to ensure effective and feasible progress within two months towards resolving the aforementioned matters through mutual consultation and negotiations.” The prime minister to form a joint political negotiating committee comprising representatives from the ruling coalition, the PPP and opposition parties. “This committee shall engage in continuous negotiations with the opposition on national and political matters, points of disagreement, and other important issues, and shall seek feasible solutions through mutual consensus. The committee shall ensure significant progress on negotiations and resolutions within one month of its formation and shall present its recommendations to the relevant leadership.” Ensuring all legal, human and medical rights for Imran and his spouse, Bushra Bibi, in accordance with the jail manual, Constitution and prevailing laws. “Where legally applicable, necessary medical facilities and treatment shall be provided to them, taking into account the opinion, instructions and advice of their personal or nominated physicians.” Allowing Imran and Bushra Bibi to meet their family members, lawyers and other associates, in accordance with the jail manual and relevant laws. “Such meetings shall be conducted in accordance with the law and jail rules and regulations. However, the facility of meetings will not be used by any party for political or other purposes prohibited by law.” The process of taking up appeals filed by prisoners against their sentences to be initiated or completed within 10 days, where legally possible, in accordance with the Constitution and law. “All cases shall be decided by the relevant courts and legal forums in accordance with the Constitution, law, transparent judicial procedures and principles of justice, without undue delay. And women who are political prisoners, including Yasmin Rashid and Bushra Bibi, should be released expeditiously on humanitarian grounds.” Effective, continuous and meaningful consultation between the federal and provincial governments to eradicate terrorism, protect the lives and property of the people and establish lasting peace in KP. “Existing policies and measures should be reviewed and amended as needed.” Authorised representatives of the federal and provincial governments shall convene regular meetings within 72 hours and, through mutual consultation, formulate a clear, comprehensive and feasible strategy for peace and security. The implementation of this strategy, within the scope of the Constitution and law, shall be the joint responsibility of the federal and provincial governments.” The KP CM said that PTI would announce the cancellation of the long march upon receiving a written assurance from the federal government for the effective implementation of the aforementioned assurances and agreed actions. “However, if the federal government violates the agreed assurances, the negotiation process, or constitutional and legal requirements, or causes undue disruption to the negotiation process, PTI shall reserve the right to peaceful, democratic and lawful protest in accordance with the Constitution and law”, he added. Responding to Afridi on X, Naqvi said the “negotiating teams finalised a separate draft with us, which both sides agreed to, in addition to the KP Terrorism Related Implementation Plan”. Commenting on that, KP Information Minister Shafiullah Jan said the PTI’s negotiating committee “came with a full mandate that we would endorse every decision they made, however they deemed fit”. “The provincial government’s mandate lies with the chief minister. The KP government’s policy cannot go against Imran Khan’s ideology. Your intent is not to end terrorism but to end PTI,” Jan asserted. “The blood of our innocent Pakhtuns is not so cheap that, under your misguided policies, we would sacrifice another 80,000 lives. Terrorism has been forcibly imposed on Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Those who start the fire can never put it out,” he claimed. The provincial minister stressed that a policy shift regarding counterterrorism was necessary as “relying solely on the policy of guns and batons will not work”. “A few self-proclaimed wise men sitting in closed rooms will not decide our future,” Jan said. PPP says KP govt ‘began dictating terms’ PPP Senator Sherry Rehman, who was part of the talks, also blamed the KP chief minister, saying the talks “collapsed on the KP government’s unilateral refusal to sign the afternoon’s pre-agreed draft on counterterrorism cooperation with the Centre”. In a post on X, she emphasised that the idea behind the agreement was to bring the province on board on all counterterrorism actions. The PPP leader said the government’s team had repeatedly asked for the provincial government of KP to be in the talks as well, but the chief minister or cabinet representatives did not turn up. “If they had a viable draft, they should have shown up themselves or communicated it to their committee over the two days, without constant reversals”, she added. “No point presenting new drafts on social media after refusing to show up or sabotaging their own teams by broadcasting messages that subvert the process,” Rehman stated. The senior politician went on to say: “I have never in my 25 years in parliament seen such a reckless squandering of an opening to begin political CBMs (confidence-building measures), and to bring stability to Pakistan after years of bitter political division.” Rehman regretted that instead of “taking the opportunity the PPP-govt team offered them to unlock the blind alley they have taken themselves into, their Peshawar government began dictating terms after 8:30pm when all but final agreements had been signed”. “We really went more than halfway. The rest could have followed.”

items.title: Israeli Authorities Trade Blame for Failure to Flag FlyDubai Co-Pilot
Australia probes flydubai co-pilot's links to the country, police say
items.description: A multi-agency Australian counterterrorism unit is investigating links to Australia of the co-pilot of flydubai flight FZ1073 , who allegedly stabbed his captain and then attempted to hijack the plane, a police spokesperson said on Sunday. The Victorian Joint Counter Terrorism Team — which comprises federal police, Victorian state police and the ASIO intelligence agency — was “investigating the man’s links to Australia”, the Australian Federal Police spokesperson said. Two sources briefed on the investigation said the co-pilot studied at a university in Melbourne, the capital of the Australian state of Victoria. A third source said he studied at RMIT University around a decade ago. RMIT declined to comment. The co-pilot of the flydubai flight FZ1073, which was bound for Israel from Dubai on Wednesday, attacked the pilot with an emergency crash axe, the United Arab Emirates’ prosecutor general said on Saturday, calling the incident a “ terrorist attack ”. Flight FZ1073 would have felt like a “ vertical roller coaster ” when it plunged 16,000 feet in about 30 seconds before being levelled out and landing safely, according to an aviation instructor who recreated the descent in a flight simulator for Reuters . Co-pilot in UAE custody Two sources have said the co-pilot is an Omani national named Hamam Al-Hamami. Israeli officials have not named the co-pilot but said that he is from Oman. UAE authorities and flydubai have not publicly disclosed the co-pilot’s identity. Reuters could not independently reach Al-Hamami, who is in UAE custody, for comment. The UAE has not announced any formal charges against him and it is not known if he has appointed legal counsel. Oman has not commented on the incident. Disaster on board flight FZ1073 was averted after passengers and crew subdued the co-pilot, who had attacked the captain in what Israeli officials said was an attempt to crash the plane carrying more than 170 passengers and crew. The UAE public prosecutor has said the co-pilot had attempted to take control of the plane. Most of the passengers on board were Israeli nationals. A reserve flydubai pilot travelling on the flight took control of the aircraft and landed it at Tabuk airport in northwestern Saudi Arabia, where the co-pilot was detained by Saudi authorities and later transferred to the UAE on Thursday. The Financial Times reported on Sunday that Al-Hamami had allegedly visited “mosques and extremist websites” while in Australia, citing two people familiar with the investigation. Australian intelligence services held a file on the individual, according to FT . Reuters could not immediately verify the FT report. The government of Australia did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside normal business hours. Netanyahu orders security review of flights Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered a security review of international flights to Israel after the incident. Netanyahu “has instructed the Head of the National Security Council, Shmuel Ben Ezra, to appoint an examiner to conduct a thorough review of all security aspects of foreign civil aviation to Israel”, a statement from the premier’s office said. Israel does not have official diplomatic relations with Oman, and Netanyahu has also claimed pilots from such countries were not permitted to operate flights to Israel. It is not clear how the co-pilot came to be assigned to the flight to Tel Aviv. Calls have mounted in Israel for an investigation into the security lapse. Transport Minister Miri Regev rejected responsibility for the failure, saying security oversight for flights operated by foreign airlines falls under the remit of the Mossad and Shin Bet, Israel’s foreign and domestic intelligence agencies. A 2024 report by the state comptroller found there was no clear division of responsibility for the security of foreign airlines operating in Israel, and recommended that the government address the issue. Israeli media has reported that pilots from countries hostile to Israel have repeatedly flown into the country in recent years. Opposition leader Yair Lapid dismissed Netanyahu’s announcement of a security review as a “sham investigation”. “The chain of failures that preceded the incident could have led to a disaster of historic proportions, and this is how an Israeli prime minister responds?” Lapid wrote on X. “Just as Netanyahu escaped an investigation into the October 7 massacre, he is now running away again,” he added. Gadi Eisenkot, a leading challenger to Netanyahu ahead of the October 27 election, wrote on X that “in a proper and functioning government, the minister of transportation would have submitted a letter of resignation last night”.

items.title: North should not use population to challenge power rotation —Yari
items.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Director-General of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul Aziz Yari Abubakar, has urged northerners not to use the region’s population to challenge the informal power-rotation arrangement in the country. He said the North should respect the political understanding that led to the emergence of President Bola Tinubu from the South in 2023 and allow him to complete his constitutionally permitted eight-year tenure. Yari made the call while speaking to journalists at Kano Government House after a meeting with the state governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf. He said the North had occupied the presidency for several years before power shifted to the South, stressing the need for Nigerians to understand and respect the political arrangement. He recalled that former President Muhammadu Buhari, a northerner, governed the country from 2015 to 2023 before Tinubu emerged as president in 2023. “From 2015 to 2023, this country was led by a northerner, and now from 2023 to 2026 it is led by a southerner,” Yari said. He, therefore, appealed to northerners not to seek to overturn the zoning arrangement because of the region’s population. “If we say we want to uproot the zoning arrangement because of our numbers, then my call for northerners is to understand how it works,” he said. “I am calling on northerners to note that by the time Bola Ahmed Tinubu finishes in 2031, it will definitely come back to the North. So, this is how the arrangement is,” he said. Yari said the political arrangement was important for national unity and should be respected by all parts of the country. He also urged Nigerians to work together to protect the country, regardless of their political or regional differences. The APC chieftain acknowledged that Tinubu’s administration was not perfect but said the challenges facing Nigeria could not all be blamed on the current government. The post North should not use population to challenge power rotation —Yari appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Train Alger – Tamanrasset : Tebboune ordonne le lancement d’un tronçon de 1500 km
items.description: Le président de la République, Abdelmadjid Tebboune, a pris ce dimanche 4 octobre, en Conseil des ministres, une décision historique en ordonnant le lancement des travaux d’un tronçon de 1581 km de la ligne ferroviaire Alger – Tamanrasset . « Le Président de la République a ordonné le lancement immédiat des projets ferroviaires relatifs aux tronçons Laghouat – Ghardaïa – El Ménéa – In Salah – Tamanrasset, les considérant comme une priorité absolue du secteur des Travaux publics, tout en exigeant une accélération globale des travaux de réalisation », a indiqué la présidence dans un communiqué publié à l’issue du Conseil des ministres. En plus du lancement des travaux, Abdelmadjid Tebboune a fixé une échéance pour la livraison de ce tronçon qui sera entièrement réalisé dans le Sahara. Il insisté sur la « nécessité d'achever l'intégralité du projet d'ici la fin de l'année 2028, permettant ainsi aux Algériens de voyager effectivement par train du Nord vers notre grand Sud, jusqu'à Tamanrasset », a ajouté la Présidence. Train Alger – Tamanrasset : l’Algérie obtient un financement de la BAD pour un tronçon de 1581 km Pour réaliser cette partie du train Alger – Tamanrasset, l’Algérie a obtenu des financements de la Banque africaine de développement. D’abord, elle a octroyé 1,5 milliard de dollars pour le tronçon Laghouat – Ghardaïa – El Ménéa sur 495 km, puis pour la partie El Ménéa – In Salah – Tamanrasset sur 1086 km, soit un total de 1581 km. Le montant de ce dernier prêt n’a pas encore été dévoilé. À la suite de l'approbation par la BAD du financement du tronçon ferroviaire pour le tronçon reliant El Ménéa à Tamanrasset, le Président de la République a chargé le ministre des Travaux publics de « transmettre ses remerciements et ses encouragements aux travailleurs, techniciens et ingénieurs du secteur ». Il a qualifié leur performance actuelle « d'héroïque à tous égards, soulignant qu'ils sont sur le point de concrétiser le rêve des Algériens, un rêve resté inaccessible pour les générations successives depuis l'indépendance. » L’article Train Alger – Tamanrasset : Tebboune ordonne le lancement d’un tronçon de 1500 km est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: France: face aux violences, jusqu’à 500 établissements scolaires fermés lundi
items.description: Les cours seront « totalement ou partiellement » suspendus lundi dans 400 à 500 établissements scolaires en France en lien avec la mobilisation des lycéens, a indiqué dimanche le ministre français de l'Éducation, Édouard Geffray. Dans des déclarations à la presse, M. Geffray a affirmé que les conditions de sécurité « ne sont pas réunies » alors que 24 établissements ont été « incendiés ou saccagés » au cours des derniers jours. « Il y aura une reprise partielle des cours de manière progressive », a ajouté le ministre qui a déploré que 78 personnels de l’éducation nationale aient été blessés depuis le début du mouvement lycéen. Les fermetures des lycées, a-t-il précisé, intervient lorsque les conditions de sécurité ne sont pas remplies, soit pour des raisons matérielles, soit parce que des personnels ont été directement visés. L'Union syndicale lycéenne (USL), l'une des composantes du mouvement de protestation lycéen, a appelé « à continuer la mobilisation en cours en l’absence de mesures concrètes » et à faire de mardi prochain une journée de manifestation nationale. Déclenché le 17 septembre dans la région parisienne, le mouvement de protestation a progressivement pris de l’ampleur au cours de la dernière semaine dans de nombreuses villes françaises. The post France: face aux violences, jusqu’à 500 établissements scolaires fermés lundi appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Goudiry : Atoumane Sy annonce son engagement aux côtés du président Bassirou Diomaye Faye
items.description: Le directeur général de l’Anaser, Atoumane Sy, a annoncé, samedi à Goudiry, son engagement politique au sein de Kiraay – Les Patriotes républicains et son soutien au président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye. Il a appelé à faire de cet engagement un moyen de mieux défendre les intérêts du département de Goudiry. Le directeur général de l’Agence nationale de l’aménagement du territoire et de l’équipement rural (Anaser), Atoumane Sy, a officiellement annoncé son engagement en politique, samedi 3 octobre, à l’occasion d’une grande rencontre organisée à Goudiry, dans le département du même nom. S’exprimant devant des responsables politiques, des autorités administratives, coutumières et religieuses, ainsi que des militants et sympathisants, M. Sy a indiqué avoir choisi de rejoindre Kiraay – Les Patriotes républicains et d’accompagner l’action du président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye. « J’ai choisi de m’engager en politique, au sein de Kiraay – Les Patriotes républicains, et d’accompagner le Président de la République », a-t-il déclaré, expliquant que cette décision procède d’une conviction et d’une volonté de prendre part à la marche du pays. Pour le responsable, l’engagement politique doit être conçu comme une forme de service public et non comme une recherche d’intérêts personnels. Fort de son expérience dans l’administration, il estime qu’il est désormais nécessaire de « prendre part » à la construction de l’avenir du Sénégal. Atoumane Sy a également expliqué les raisons de son choix de Kiraay. Il a mis en avant les valeurs de patriotisme et de républicanisme qu’il associe à cette formation politique, notamment la primauté de l’intérêt général, le respect des institutions et l’égale dignité des citoyens. Évoquant le président Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye, il a salué « un homme de devoir », de « sobriété et d’humilité », ainsi qu’un responsable attaché au dialogue, à la rigueur et au service de l’État. Selon lui, accompagner le chef de l’État ne saurait se limiter à l’applaudir, mais doit également consister à relayer les préoccupations des populations et à contribuer à la concrétisation des orientations nationales. « Accompagner un Président, ce n’est pas applaudir. C’est porter une part du fardeau. C’est être loyal sans être courtisan », a-t-il notamment soutenu. Défendre les intérêts de Goudiry Une large partie de son intervention a été consacrée aux perspectives du département de Goudiry. Atoumane Sy estime que le territoire doit occuper une place plus importante dans les politiques publiques nationales. « Le département de Goudiry n’a pas à demander une faveur. Il demande sa place », a-t-il affirmé, citant notamment les enjeux liés à l’agriculture, à l’élevage, au commerce, à l’éducation et à l’accès aux services sociaux de base. Il a exprimé le souhait de voir émerger un territoire où les jeunes pourraient réussir sans être contraints de quitter leur localité, où les femmes bénéficieraient de meilleures conditions pour développer leurs activités et où les agriculteurs et les éleveurs pourraient davantage tirer profit de leur travail. Sans promettre de solutions immédiates, le responsable a plutôt misé sur la constance et la proximité. « Je ne vous promets pas des miracles. Les miracles n’appartiennent pas à la politique. Je vous promets de la constance, de la présence et de la fidélité », a-t-il déclaré. Atoumane Sy a, par ailleurs, appelé à préserver l’unité sociale dans le département, estimant que les divergences politiques ne doivent pas remettre en cause les liens familiaux et communautaires. Il a tendu la main à ceux qui ne partagent pas encore son choix politique, en insistant sur l’importance du débat et du respect. « Nous resterons une seule communauté », a-t-il lancé, avant d’appeler les populations à juger son engagement sur ses actes et dans la durée. La rencontre s’est achevée par un appel à l’unité autour du développement de Goudiry et à l’accompagnement de l’action du président de la République. Atoumane Sy a réaffirmé sa volonté de porter la voix du département dans les espaces où sont définies les orientations publiques nationales.

La Policía empieza a desalojar el asentamiento de migrantes de la playa de El Trampolín de Ceuta
items.description: La Policía Nacional ha desalojado parcialmente el asentamiento de migrantes de la playa de El Trampolín , en Ceuta, con un imponente operativo desplegado este domingo. Tras una noche sin presencia policial, sobre las 7.30 ha llegado la primera furgoneta de la Unidad de Intervención Policial (UIP) para una toma de contacto inicial. Aún no había amanecido, la bruma cubría el mar y la mayoría de migrantes seguían durmiendo. Minutos después, un dron ha empezado a sobrevolar la zona y, finalmente, el amplio dispositivo ha arrancado por sorpresa ya a las 8.00. A esa hora, medio centenar de furgonetas de la Policía Nacional, tres tanquetas de los antidisturbios y otra decena de vehículos pesados del Ejército han irrumpido entre la neblina, todos de golpe, para perimetrar los accesos y dividir el poblado en varios sectores. El dispositivo duró unas 12 horas, en las que los agentes estuvieron llevándose a grupos de gente. Varios inmigrantes intentaron escapar por el agua. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Tomate : le Maroc devance de nouveau l'Espagne dans l'UE
items.description: Deuxième fournisseur de tomates de l'Union européenne en 2025/2026, le Royaume passe devant l'Espagne pour la deuxième année d'affilée. Sur dix campagnes, ses exportations ont progressé de plus de 22%, alors que celles de ses concurrents ibérique et néerlandais ont reculé. Sur le marché européen de la tomate, le rapport de forces continue de pencher en faveur du Maroc. Lors de la campagne 2025/2026, le Royaume a écoulé dans l'Union européenne (UE) des volumes supérieurs à ceux de l'Espagne, ce qui se produit pour la deuxième année consécutive. Ce constat ressort d'une analyse du site spécialisé Hortoinfo, qui s'appuie sur les données du service statistique Euroestacom (Icex-Eurostat). Le Maroc conforte ainsi sa deuxième place parmi les fournisseurs de l'Union, derrière les Pays-Bas. Cette performance s'inscrit dans une dynamique de fond. Si l'on compare la campagne 2025/2026 à celle de 2016/2017, les expéditions marocaines vers l'UE affichent une hausse de 22,17%, passant de 403.798 à 493.327 tonnes. Sur la même période, les ventes espagnoles ont reculé de 36,99%, revenant de 755.175 à 475.803 tonnes, et celles des Pays-Bas de 18,4%, de 947.852 à 773.449 tonnes. Pour cette campagne, les États membres ont acheté plus de 2,78 millions de tonnes de tomates, pour une facture dépassant 5,56 milliards d'euros. Le prix moyen payé ressort à deux euros le kilo. À titre de comparaison, le volume total importé atteignait 3,07 millions de tonnes en 2016/2017, soit un recul global de 9,33% en dix campagnes. Les Pays-Bas restent en tête du classement, malgré leur repli sur dix campagnes. Leurs exportateurs ont placé 773.450 tonnes, soit 27,81% du volume total importé, pour une valeur de plus de 1,64 milliard d'euros. Le kilo s'est vendu en moyenne à 2,13 euros. Le Maroc vient juste derrière, avec 493.330 tonnes, soit 17,74% du volume total. Ces ventes ont généré 1,03 milliard d'euros, sur la base d'un prix moyen de 2,09 euros le kilo. L'Espagne talonne son voisin du sud avec 475.800 tonnes, soit 17,11% du volume global, pour 1,01 milliard d'euros. Son prix moyen, de 2,14 euros le kilo, dépasse celui obtenu par les producteurs marocains. Le Portugal occupe la quatrième place avec 175.020 tonnes, pour 117,58 millions d'euros seulement. Son prix moyen, de 0,67 euro le kilo, est nettement inférieur à celui de ses concurrents, car l'essentiel de ses livraisons concerne des tomates destinées à l'industrie. Ses ventes ont toutefois bondi de 171,02% depuis 2016/2017. La France complète le top 5 avec 160.750 tonnes, pour une valeur de 373,31 millions d'euros. Ses ventes ont cédé 13,53% sur dix campagnes, mais elle affiche le prix moyen le plus élevé des cinq principaux fournisseurs, à 2,32 euros le kilo. Derrière ce quintette, la Turquie a livré 148.411 tonnes (5,34% du total), en hausse de 49,68% sur dix campagnes, devant la Belgique avec 141.470 tonnes, en recul de 26,24%. L'Allemagne et l'Italie ont respectivement fourni 104.768 et 68.349 tonnes, tandis que la Tunisie, avec 38.918 tonnes, a vu ses volumes multipliés par plus de quatre (+310,85%). The post Tomate : le Maroc devance de nouveau l'Espagne dans l'UE appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Yemen presidency announces military drive to retake all territory seized by Houthis
items.description: Yemen’s leader announced on Sunday the start of a new military operation to retake all territory held by the Houthis, even as the group made fresh gains on the ground, effectively encircling a government-held city. The announcement sets an ambitious goal for the embattled government, which recently lost swathes of the country’s Red Sea coastline and areas around the Bab al-Mandab strait — a chokepoint for international shipping — after a lightning offensive by Houthis. Yemen’s government has struggled to roll back the surge, even with the military support of Saudi Arabia, where the Houthis said they had attacked oil infrastructure in the capital yet again on Sunday. “I announce today the start of military operations to retake the remaining territories of the republic and extend the authority of the state and its institutions across the entire national territory,” Rashad al-Alimi, the head of Yemen’s presidential council, said in a statement. Alimi called on all the armed forces “to begin carrying out their assigned missions, in accordance with the approved plans, until the country is liberated from the grip of the Houthi terrorist militia”. The statement came just hours after the Houthis cut a vital supply route linking the besieged city of Taiz with the government’s interim capital Aden, according to four security sources. The Houthi advance followed days of heavy fighting in and around Taiz, where dozens of combatants were reported killed on Friday. The battle for Taiz is taking place on several fronts, including highlands overlooking coastal areas recently seized by the Houthis. Taiz is Yemen’s third-largest city after Sanaa and Aden. “We were informed that the Houthis had taken control of the al-Safiya area, where they cut the main road and took control of the police station,” a police source in the area told AFP . Three sources with the Yemeni military also confirmed Houthi control over the area and the supply route, with traffic along the road halted and the group now surrounding Taiz city. The military sources added that fighting in the area was ongoing. Sources from both sides told AFP on Sunday that fighting in and around the western province of Taiz has killed more than 70 people over the past day. Sources from the internationally recognised government reported that 34 government troops were killed — 20 on the edge of Taiz province in neighbouring Lahj — while Houthi military sources said 39 of their fighters were killed in fighting across Taiz and in border areas with Lahj. Taiz city itself remains under the control of government forces but has long been besieged from the north, east and west by Houthi fighters and remains one of the main fronts in Yemen’s long-running civil war. “They’ve achieved the military objective of isolating Taiz from Aden, even if they haven’t fully taken control of it,” Farea Al-Muslimi, research fellow at the Chatham House think-tank, told AFP . Muslimi also downplayed expectations over what the coming government offensive might accomplish. “In my opinion, it’s meaningless,” he added. But Taiz residents vowed to resist any Houthi advance. “We will defeat and crush anyone who enters the city of Taiz. We will not abandon Taiz,” resident Zakaria Al-Dhubhani said. “This is a message to the Houthis: I swear to God, we will not allow you to advance a single inch into the city.” Saudi attacks Following several years of relative calm, Yemen’s civil war reignited in July against the backdrop of the wider conflict in the Middle East. It has also drawn in Saudi Arabia — leader of an anti-Houthi military coalition since 2015 — with the group regularly claiming attacks on the kingdom’s territory in recent weeks and declaring a blockade of its ships in the Red Sea. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree on Sunday said the group launched ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi energy giant Aramco’s sites in Riyadh and in the oil-rich Khurais area in the east. “The strikes were precise, causing large fires at the targeted sites,” Saree said on X. Saudi oil exports were already under pressure thanks to Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz in the Gulf. The Houthis’ Al-Masirah TV channel reported Saudi strikes on Sunday in the northern governorates of al-Jawf and Saada, saying at least two people had been wounded. They came a day after Yemen’s government said its forces struck Houthi targets around the country, including in the capital Sanaa, the northwestern governorate of Saada and the group’s positions near Taiz in the southwest. The Yemeni government’s air capabilities, however, are limited, and the Saudi-led coalition has long been the primary force carrying out airstrikes against the Houthis. Experts believe the recent operations have most likely been conducted by Saudi warplanes as well. Yemen is one of the poorest countries in the world and remains gripped by a vast humanitarian crisis that has unspooled since the civil war broke out in 2014. That year the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa from the Saudi-led government, before going on to take control of much of the country’s north, with Riyadh’s international coalition intervening the following year. Hunger warning Hostilities between the Houthis and Yemen’s government had reignited after four years of a fragile truce when Iran sent a plane to Sanaa carrying a Houthi delegation. The flight did not seek authorisation from Saudi Arabia, contravening a practice in place for a decade. Riyadh retaliated with strikes on Sanaa airport, and in response the Houthis attacked Saudi territory for the first time since 2022. Since then, fighting has intensified with the Houthis launching a lightning offensive in which they seized control of coastal regions along the Bab al-Mandab strait. They have also struck multiple Saudi targets including oil infrastructure and the capital Riyadh while also announcing a naval blockade on Saudi shipping in the Red Sea. The renewed fighting has worsened a humanitarian crisis sweeping Yemen, with the World Food Programme warning on Friday that three-quarters of the population was unable to meet its basic food needs.
